# Native Wrist Kinematic Compatibility (Provisional)

## Scope and Evidence Boundary

F07 child #11834 supplies `tour_matching.observe_native_wrist`, an executable
native geometry assay before donor assembly. It reuses the public model
checkpoint and path-length finite-difference providers. The existing F07 asset
inventory (#11819) remains the structural inventory boundary; this assay does
not duplicate it or claim complete component coverage from a selected path list.
All results have `scientific_status="unqualified"`. No third-party anatomy,
capture or display mesh is included in the synthetic test fixture.

This assay does not integrate dynamics, prepare muscle equilibrium, fit a
capture or build an anatomical derivative. Donor compatibility needs a reviewed
registration and comparison against a proposed derivative. A source measured
against itself does not establish that assembly.

## Frames, Coordinates and Native Assembly

The contract names exact native independent/dependent coordinate paths, muscle
paths, required components, anchor and hand frames, poses and numerical
tolerances. Requested wrist values are declared in radians. Native rotational
coordinates are admitted directly; native `Coupled` coordinates require an
explicit `declared_coupled_radian_coordinates` entry grounded in the source
functions and their units. This declaration is recorded, not anatomically
certified. Native translational input coordinates are rejected.

OpenSim [CustomJoint motion classification](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/4.6/OpenSim/Simulation/SimbodyEngine/CustomJoint.cpp)
can mark scaled/nonlinear rotation functions as `Coupled`; the enum is not
equivalent to a coordinate-coupler constraint. The assay separately checks
`Coordinate.isDependent(state)`. It never changes those functions or relabels
the native enum to make an input pass.

Each sample copies the initialized native state, sets all requested coordinates
without intermediate enforcement, calls `Model.assemble`, and realizes
Position. All achieved native coordinates and position-constraint errors are
recorded. Independent coordinates outside the requested set must stay at their
baseline values within the declared angular or translational tolerance.
Requested coordinates must achieve their values and remain inside native ranges.
Missing components, locked/prescribed inputs, disabled required constraints,
unsupported held-coordinate motion types and non-finite observations fail.
Required component dumps retain exact native coupler/wrap/joint settings.

The returned transform maps hand-frame coordinates into the anchor frame:

$$X_{AH}=X_{GA}^{-1}X_{GH}.$$

Its translation is in meters and its rotation is dimensionless. Neither frame
names nor this transform alone establish homologous anatomical registration.

## Path Derivatives and Numerical Policy

For each pose, independent coordinate, muscle and strictly decreasing positive
step $h$, the assay reassembles both sides. It records native
`Muscle.computeMomentArm` and the constrained path derivative

$$r_{\mathrm{FD}}=-\frac{\ell_{MT}(q^+)-\ell_{MT}(q^-)}
{q_i^+-q_i^-}.$$

The denominator uses achieved coordinates. Steps must exceed the coordinate
tolerance. Every stencil retains all achieved coordinates, path lengths and
constraint errors, allowing detection of motion in other coordinates or
changes in wrapping. The sign convention is the negative length derivative;
with the declared angular coordinates the result is meters per radian, normally
reported as a moment-arm length in meters. The native generalized-force and
moving-path semantics must be examined when these disagree; a small numerical
residual is not a physiological capacity check.

`assembly_accuracy=None` preserves the model's numerical setting. An explicitly
requested value calls native `Model.set_assembly_accuracy` before initialization.
The receipt binds source/default/requested/effective policy, pre-policy model
serialization, prepared model serialization, source-file SHA-256, provider
source hashes, native version and loaded extension hashes. Transitive DLL and
external resource closure remain unverified. File bytes and prepared parameters
are rechecked after observation. Numerical policy is never changed silently;
an explicit accuracy override does not edit anatomical parameters. Native loader
transformations still require admission review: this donor reports a massless
thorax with nonzero inertia and resets that inertia. Loaded identity does not
prove equality to the source's declared physical properties.

`within_declared_tolerance` is reported for each comparison; disagreement is
retained without raising or promoting a qualified status. The numerical
tolerance is an operator declaration, not a measured uncertainty. Changing
the tolerance after inspecting results cannot establish preregistered acceptance.
Finite differences need explicit refinement and differentiation-path evidence,
particularly for analytic wraps and coordinate-dependent moving path points.

## Pinned Donor Findings and Remaining Gates

The local evaluation used `MOBL_ARMS_41.osim` at CEINMS-RT/UpperLimbModel commit
`459e2ebbf47acb72b0ecbc59950a2d0a983d28db`, SHA-256
`58bacbc1c61d1d42cff9a48b0a9dced9c648893f44adc7d9817cca56441a9fcf`,
in native OpenSim `4.6-2026-06-22-85aaf64`. Its
[artifact-specific notices](https://github.com/CEINMS-RT/UpperLimbModel/blob/459e2ebbf47acb72b0ecbc59950a2d0a983d28db/README.md)
separate the MoBL model from Apache-licensed code and restrict the model's
listed uses to noncommercial research, academic, evaluation or personal use;
commercial use requires its stated licensing route. Older catalog MIT entries
do not establish identity or broad redistribution rights for this exact file.
Keep original notices, citations and geometry/version provenance.

The donor chain is `/jointset/radiocarpal` (radius to proximal_row) followed by
`/jointset/wrist_hand` (proximal_row to hand). Preserve
`/constraintset/wrist_hand_r1_con` and `/constraintset/wrist_hand_r3_con`, all
selected paths and passive forces. ECRL uses
`/bodyset/humerus/wrapobjectset/Elbow_PT_ECRL` (ellipsoid) and
`/bodyset/proximal_row/wrapobjectset/ECRL` (torus). These are analytic wraps,
distinct from missing display meshes. Donor flexion/deviation are natively
`Coupled` because of their spline transforms; their declared angular input
domains must be preserved.

An unchanged-source default-accuracy run failed the $10^{-7}$-rad isolation
gate: elbow flexion moved by $9.52935\times10^{-6}$ rad at a wrist stencil.
Explicit accuracy refinement from $10^{-9}$ through $10^{-14}$ reduced the
observed maximum held-coordinate drift at the two initial test samples to
$2.55629\times10^{-8}$ rad, passing the same isolation gate. Both direct
`Model.assemble` and coordinate `setValue(..., True)` produced the same result
in that controlled comparison. Native assembly accuracy is not itself a bound
on coordinate drift.

The separate $10^{-14}$-accuracy run completed 432 comparisons: 3 poses, 24
hand-reaching muscles, 2 wrist coordinates and 3 steps ($10^{-3}$, $10^{-4}$,
$10^{-5}$ rad). Of these, 180 exceeded the predeclared $10^{-5}$-m diagnostic
tolerance. Neutral ECRL/deviation retained a 0.199353-mm discrepancy. The
largest was FPL/flexion at $(0.1,0.05)$ rad: native 9.67396 mm versus finite
difference 14.81422 mm, with about 5.14026-mm disagreement persisting under
step refinement. These are unresolved geometry/generalized-force/derivative
gates, not proof of a particular runtime bug. The complete receipts remain in
the local planning evaluation folder; no foreign asset is redistributed here.

Before anatomical splicing, compare the preserved donor and proposed derivative
under explicit frame registration, all coordinate/coupler conventions, native
hand transforms, path lengths, analytic wraps, moment arms and capacity over a
reviewed workspace. Include the moving-path functions in the derivative audit;
OpenSim documents [their coordinate-dependent locations and derivatives](https://opensim-org.github.io/opensim-moco-site/docs/1.3.0/html_user/classOpenSim_1_1MovingPathPoint.html).
No mass or muscle may be counted twice, and left-side mirroring needs separate
axis/inertia/handedness validation. A rigid hand with extrinsic paths does not
qualify articulated-finger recruitment, grip strength, slip or club contact.

F07/F08 still require native muscle law/state policies, assistance disposition,
contact/grip readiness, frozen real-capture protocol, coupled identification and
full-horizon independently restored excitation replay under model-owned contact.
The accepted milestone DAG and model/engine denominator are unchanged.

## Verification and Reproduction

Use an installed native OpenSim Python provider and run serially:

```sh
python3 -m pytest -o addopts='' tests/opensim/test_native_wrist_compatibility.py tests/scripts/test_design_manual_governance_contract.py -q
python3 -m scripts.check_design_manual_governance
```

The original synthetic fixture exercises native two-stage coupling, relative
hand rotation, active wrap-radius effects, locks/prescription/disabled couplers,
range checks, actual requested and held values, explicit numerical policy and
scaled CustomJoint unit declarations. Intentional native-state corruption
tests the rejection guards; those injected failures are not donor evidence.
The scaled rotational synthetic moment arm agrees with its path derivative,
so the `Coupled` enum alone does not explain the donor disagreement. Tests skip
native cases when OpenSim is unavailable; skips do not qualify the provider.
The engineering-manual release remains blocked pending governed inventory,
rendering, evidence and review.
